payload.recallText: It's a story about a young lady named Mykala (don't think it's the correct spelling) who was related to the Kennedy family. She spoke about how much the families had in common. Both lived in the same area. Both families were Catholics, etc. However, because the political Kennedy family was so busy they didn't see one another. Although they did love each other. Once when Mykala was in the car and heard a report about the death of JFK, she started to cry. Her brother told their dad that she was crying. The dad pulled over the car and comforted his daughter by telling her it's okay to cry for him and to never ashamed of crying for JFK. Once when the families were on separate vacations, close, but not near each other Mykala and her siblings/cousins went out on the water and had to be rescued by two of the Kennedy boys. The older relatives were not pleased that they had gone so far out into the water.
